_doc: Language-neutral conformance fixture for the empty-hour dwell statistics. The corpus side (mogwai-lab's `characterize::dwell_stats`) measures the archives and the synthetic side (mogwai-data's `empty_hour_stats_over`) measures the generated tape, and a realism gate compares one against the other. The two implementations are deliberately separate - they work in different units and the lab side carries an era clamp the generator has no use for - so 'the gate compares like with like' would otherwise rest on two implementations happening to agree bucket for bucket. Running this fixture through both turns that into a tested contract. Keep the implementations separate; keep this fixture shared.

units.first_ts_s: seconds after `epoch`, the instant of the first print
units.last_ts_s: seconds after `epoch`, the instant of the last print
units.occupied_hours: whole-hour indices after `epoch`, one per hour holding at least one print
units.empty_hour_frac: empty complete hours divided by complete hours
units.max_empty_hour_run_h: hours in the longest unbroken run of empty complete hours

epoch.why: the dwell era start, 2019-01-01T00:00:00Z, and an exact multiple of 3600. Cases are stated as offsets from it so that the lab side's clamp of `first_ts` to the era start is a no-op for every case here, which is what lets one fixture drive an implementation that clamps and one that does not. The clamp itself is lab-local and is pinned lab-side.

rules.population: every COMPLETE hour bucket lying fully inside [first_ts, last_ts]: the first is ceil(first_ts/3600) and the last is floor(last_ts/3600) - 1
rules.partial_buckets: the buckets holding first_ts and last_ts are excluded from the population unless they happen to be complete, and prints inside an excluded bucket are ignored entirely - they neither occupy nor count
rules.empty_span: a span holding no complete bucket defines BOTH statistics as zero, which keeps the helper total rather than fallible
rules.run_length: the longest run is a maximum over runs, so a later shorter run never displaces it, and a run still open at the last complete hour counts at its full length

cases.name: partial_edges_are_excluded
cases.why: the base case: prints straddle both edges, so the population is the two whole hours between them

cases.name: no_complete_bucket_in_the_span
cases.why: under an hour of complete coverage defines both statistics as zero rather than dividing by zero

cases.name: last_bucket_ends_exactly_on_the_final_print
cases.why: a final print landing exactly on an hour boundary completes the bucket before it, so hours 0 through 4 are the population and only hour 0 is occupied

cases.name: every_complete_hour_occupied
cases.why: a dense tape reports no emptiness and no run at all

cases.name: longest_run_is_a_maximum_not_the_last
cases.why: a three-hour desert followed by a two-hour one must report three; an implementation reporting the most recent run reports two

cases.name: a_run_open_at_the_end_counts_in_full
cases.why: the final run is never closed by a subsequent occupied hour, so an implementation that only records a run when it ends loses it

cases.name: single_complete_bucket
cases.why: the minimal non-degenerate population, and it is entirely empty

cases.name: prints_in_the_partial_buckets_do_not_occupy
cases.why: occupancy is read only over the population; prints in the excluded edge buckets must not rescue the complete hours between them from being empty
